clauses.normalized_text: This document describes loss detection and congestion control mechanisms for QUIC.
clauses.raw_text: This document describes loss detection and congestion control mechanisms for QUIC.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC is a new multiplexed and secure transport atop UDP.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC is a new multiplexed and secure transport atop UDP.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC builds on decades of transport and security experience, and implements mechanisms that make it attractive as a modern general-purpose transport.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC builds on decades of transport and security experience, and implements mechanisms that make it attractive as a modern general-purpose transport.

clauses.normalized_text: The QUIC protocol is described in [QUIC-TRANSPORT].

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC implements the spirit of known TCP loss recovery mechanisms, described in RFCs, various Internet-drafts, and also those prevalent in the Linux TCP implementation.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC implements the spirit of known TCP loss recovery mechanisms, described in RFCs, various Internet-drafts, and also those prevalent in the Linux TCP implementation.

clauses.raw_text: Definitions of terms that are used in this document:

clauses.normalized_text: ACK frames:: ACK frames refer to both ACK and ACK_ECN frames in this document.

clauses.normalized_text: ACK-only:: Any packet containing only an ACK or ACK_ECN frame.
clauses.raw_text: ACK-only:: Any packet containing only an ACK or ACK_ECN frame.

clauses.normalized_text: In-flight:: Packets are considered in-flight when they have been sent and neither acknowledged nor declared lost, and they are not ACK-only.
clauses.raw_text: In-flight:: Packets are considered in-flight when they have been sent and neither acknowledged nor declared lost, and they are not ACK-only.

clauses.normalized_text: Retransmittable Frames:: All frames besides ACK, ACK_ECN, or PADDING are considered retransmittable.
clauses.raw_text: Retransmittable Frames:: All frames besides ACK, ACK_ECN, or PADDING are considered retransmittable.

clauses.raw_text: Retransmittable Packets:: Packets that contain retransmittable frames elicit an ACK from the receiver and are called retransmittable packets.

clauses.normalized_text: All transmissions in QUIC are sent with a packet-level header, which indicates the encryption level and includes a packet sequence number (referred to below as a packet number).

clauses.raw_text: Packet numbers never repeat within a packet number space for the lifetime of a connection.

clauses.normalized_text: Packet numbers monotonically increase within a space, preventing ambiguity.

clauses.normalized_text: This design obviates the need for disambiguating between transmissions and retransmissions and eliminates significant complexity from QUIC’s interpretation of TCP loss detection mechanisms.
clauses.raw_text: This design obviates the need for disambiguating between transmissions and retransmissions and eliminates significant complexity from QUIC’s interpretation of TCP loss detection mechanisms.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC packets can contain multiple frames of different types.

clauses.normalized_text: All packets are acknowledged, though packets that contain only ACK, ACK_ECN, and PADDING frames are not acknowledged immediately.
clauses.raw_text: All packets are acknowledged, though packets that contain only ACK, ACK_ECN, and PADDING frames are not acknowledged immediately.
clauses.section_heading: Design of the QUIC Transmission Machinery

clauses.normalized_text: Long header packets that contain CRYPTO frames are critical to the performance of the QUIC handshake and use shorter timers for acknowledgement and retransmission.
clauses.raw_text: Long header packets that contain CRYPTO frames are critical to the performance of the QUIC handshake and use shorter timers for acknowledgement and retransmission.
clauses.section_heading: Design of the QUIC Transmission Machinery

clauses.normalized_text: Packets that contain only ACK and ACK_ECN frames do not count toward congestion control limits and are not considered in-flight.
clauses.raw_text: Packets that contain only ACK and ACK_ECN frames do not count toward congestion control limits and are not considered in-flight.

clauses.normalized_text: Note that this means PADDING frames cause packets to contribute toward bytes in flight without directly causing an acknowledgment to be sent.
clauses.raw_text: Note that this means PADDING frames cause packets to contribute toward bytes in flight without directly causing an acknowledgment to be sent.

clauses.normalized_text: Readers familiar with TCP’s loss detection and congestion control will find algorithms here that parallel well-known TCP ones.
clauses.raw_text: Readers familiar with TCP’s loss detection and congestion control will find algorithms here that parallel well-known TCP ones.
clauses.section_heading: Relevant Differences Between QUIC and TCP

clauses.normalized_text: Protocol differences between QUIC and TCP however contribute to algorithmic differences.
clauses.raw_text: Protocol differences between QUIC and TCP however contribute to algorithmic differences.
clauses.section_heading: Relevant Differences Between QUIC and TCP

clauses.normalized_text: We briefly describe these protocol differences below.
clauses.raw_text: We briefly describe these protocol differences below.
clauses.section_heading: Relevant Differences Between QUIC and TCP

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC uses separate packet number spaces for each encryption level, except 0-RTT and all generations of 1-RTT keys use the same packet number space.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC uses separate packet number spaces for each encryption level, except 0-RTT and all generations of 1-RTT keys use the same packet number space.

clauses.normalized_text: Separate packet number spaces ensures acknowledgement of packets sent with one level of encryption will not cause spurious retransmission of packets sent with a different encryption level.
clauses.raw_text: Separate packet number spaces ensures acknowledgement of packets sent with one level of encryption will not cause spurious retransmission of packets sent with a different encryption level.

clauses.normalized_text: Congestion control and RTT measurement are unified across packet number spaces.
clauses.raw_text: Congestion control and RTT measurement are unified across packet number spaces.

clauses.normalized_text: TCP conflates transmission sequence number at the sender with delivery sequence number at the receiver, which results in retransmissions of the same data carrying the same sequence number, and consequently to problems caused by “retransmission ambiguity”.
clauses.raw_text: TCP conflates transmission sequence number at the sender with delivery sequence number at the receiver, which results in retransmissions of the same data carrying the same sequence number, and consequently to problems caused by “retransmission ambiguity”.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC separates the two: QUIC uses a packet number for transmissions, and any application data is sent in one or more streams, with delivery order determined by stream offsets encoded within STREAM frames.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC separates the two: QUIC uses a packet number for transmissions, and any application data is sent in one or more streams, with delivery order determined by stream offsets encoded within STREAM frames.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC’s packet number is strictly increasing, and directly encodes transmission order.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC’s packet number is strictly increasing, and directly encodes transmission order.

clauses.normalized_text: A higher QUIC packet number signifies that the packet was sent later, and a lower QUIC packet number signifies that the packet was sent earlier.
clauses.raw_text: A higher QUIC packet number signifies that the packet was sent later, and a lower QUIC packet number signifies that the packet was sent earlier.

clauses.normalized_text: When a packet containing frames is deemed lost, QUIC rebundles necessary frames in a new packet with a new packet number, removing ambiguity about which packet is acknowledged when an ACK is received.
clauses.raw_text: When a packet containing frames is deemed lost, QUIC rebundles necessary frames in a new packet with a new packet number, removing ambiguity about which packet is acknowledged when an ACK is received.

clauses.normalized_text: Consequently, more accurate RTT measurements can be made, spurious retransmissions are trivially detected, and mechanisms such as Fast Retransmit can be applied universally, based only on packet number.
clauses.raw_text: Consequently, more accurate RTT measurements can be made, spurious retransmissions are trivially detected, and mechanisms such as Fast Retransmit can be applied universally, based only on packet number.

clauses.normalized_text: This design point significantly simplifies loss detection mechanisms for QUIC.
clauses.raw_text: This design point significantly simplifies loss detection mechanisms for QUIC.

clauses.normalized_text: Most TCP mechanisms implicitly attempt to infer transmission ordering based on TCP sequence numbers - a non-trivial task, especially when TCP timestamps are not available.
clauses.raw_text: Most TCP mechanisms implicitly attempt to infer transmission ordering based on TCP sequence numbers - a non-trivial task, especially when TCP timestamps are not available.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC ACKs contain information that is similar to TCP SACK, but QUIC does not allow any acked packet to be reneged, greatly simplifying implementations on both sides and reducing memory pressure on the sender.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC ACKs contain information that is similar to TCP SACK, but QUIC does not allow any acked packet to be reneged, greatly simplifying implementations on both sides and reducing memory pressure on the sender.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC supports many ACK ranges, opposed to TCP’s 3 SACK ranges.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC supports many ACK ranges, opposed to TCP’s 3 SACK ranges.

clauses.normalized_text: In high loss environments, this speeds recovery, reduces spurious retransmits, and ensures forward progress without relying on timeouts.
clauses.raw_text: In high loss environments, this speeds recovery, reduces spurious retransmits, and ensures forward progress without relying on timeouts.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC ACKs explicitly encode the delay incurred at the receiver between when a packet is received and when the corresponding ACK is sent.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC ACKs explicitly encode the delay incurred at the receiver between when a packet is received and when the corresponding ACK is sent.

clauses.normalized_text: This allows the receiver of the ACK to adjust for receiver delays, specifically the delayed ack timer, when estimating the path RTT.
clauses.raw_text: This allows the receiver of the ACK to adjust for receiver delays, specifically the delayed ack timer, when estimating the path RTT.

clauses.normalized_text: This mechanism also allows a receiver to measure and report the delay from when a packet was received by the OS kernel, which is useful in receivers which may incur delays such as context-switch latency before a userspace QUIC receiver processes a received packet.
clauses.raw_text: This mechanism also allows a receiver to measure and report the delay from when a packet was received by the OS kernel, which is useful in receivers which may incur delays such as context-switch latency before a userspace QUIC receiver processes a received packet.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC senders use both ack information and timeouts to detect lost packets, and this section provides a description of these algorithms.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC senders use both ack information and timeouts to detect lost packets, and this section provides a description of these algorithms.

clauses.normalized_text: Estimating the network round-trip time (RTT) is critical to these algorithms and is described first.
clauses.raw_text: Estimating the network round-trip time (RTT) is critical to these algorithms and is described first.

clauses.normalized_text: RTT is calculated when an ACK frame arrives by computing the difference between the current time and the time the largest newly acked packet was sent.
clauses.raw_text: RTT is calculated when an ACK frame arrives by computing the difference between the current time and the time the largest newly acked packet was sent.

clauses.normalized_text: If no packets are newly acknowledged, RTT cannot be calculated. When RTT is calculated, the ack delay field from the ACK frame SHOULD be subtracted from the RTT as long as the result is larger than the Min RTT.
clauses.raw_text: If no packets are newly acknowledged, RTT cannot be calculated. When RTT is calculated, the ack delay field from the ACK frame SHOULD be subtracted from the RTT as long as the result is larger than the Min RTT.

clauses.normalized_text: If the result is smaller than the min_rtt, the RTT should be used, but the ack delay field should be ignored.
clauses.raw_text: If the result is smaller than the min_rtt, the RTT should be used, but the ack delay field should be ignored.

clauses.normalized_text: Like TCP, QUIC calculates both smoothed RTT and RTT variance similar to those specified in [RFC6298].
clauses.raw_text: Like TCP, QUIC calculates both smoothed RTT and RTT variance similar to those specified in [RFC6298].

clauses.normalized_text: Min RTT is the minimum RTT measured over the connection, prior to adjusting by ack delay.
clauses.raw_text: Min RTT is the minimum RTT measured over the connection, prior to adjusting by ack delay.

clauses.normalized_text: Ignoring ack delay for min RTT prevents intentional or unintentional underestimation of min RTT, which in turn prevents underestimating smoothed RTT.
clauses.raw_text: Ignoring ack delay for min RTT prevents intentional or unintentional underestimation of min RTT, which in turn prevents underestimating smoothed RTT.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC is able to explicitly model delay at the receiver via the ack delay field in the ACK frame.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC is able to explicitly model delay at the receiver via the ack delay field in the ACK frame.

clauses.normalized_text: Therefore, QUIC diverges from TCP by calculating a MaxAckDelay dynamically, instead of assuming a constant delayed ack timeout for all connections.
clauses.raw_text: Therefore, QUIC diverges from TCP by calculating a MaxAckDelay dynamically, instead of assuming a constant delayed ack timeout for all connections.

clauses.normalized_text: MaxAckDelay is the maximum ack delay supplied in an all incoming ACK frames.
clauses.raw_text: MaxAckDelay is the maximum ack delay supplied in an all incoming ACK frames.

clauses.normalized_text: MaxAckDelay excludes ack delays that aren’t included in an RTT sample because they’re too large or the largest acknowledged has already been acknowledged.
clauses.raw_text: MaxAckDelay excludes ack delays that aren’t included in an RTT sample because they’re too large or the largest acknowledged has already been acknowledged.

clauses.normalized_text: MaxAckDelay also excludes ack delays where the largest acknowledged references an ACK-only packet.
clauses.raw_text: MaxAckDelay also excludes ack delays where the largest acknowledged references an ACK-only packet.

clauses.normalized_text: Ack-based loss detection implements the spirit of TCP’s Fast Retransmit [RFC5681], Early Retransmit [RFC5827], FACK, and SACK loss recovery [RFC6675].
clauses.raw_text: Ack-based loss detection implements the spirit of TCP’s Fast Retransmit [RFC5681], Early Retransmit [RFC5827], FACK, and SACK loss recovery [RFC6675].

clauses.normalized_text: This section provides an overview of how these algorithms are implemented in QUIC.
clauses.raw_text: This section provides an overview of how these algorithms are implemented in QUIC.

clauses.normalized_text: An unacknowledged packet is marked as lost when an acknowledgment is received for a packet that was sent a threshold number of packets (kReorderingThreshold) and/or a threshold amount of time after the unacknowledged packet.
clauses.raw_text: An unacknowledged packet is marked as lost when an acknowledgment is received for a packet that was sent a threshold number of packets (kReorderingThreshold) and/or a threshold amount of time after the unacknowledged packet.

clauses.normalized_text: Receipt of the acknowledgement indicates that a later packet was received, while the reordering threshold provides some tolerance for reordering of packets in the network.
clauses.raw_text: Receipt of the acknowledgement indicates that a later packet was received, while the reordering threshold provides some tolerance for reordering of packets in the network.

clauses.normalized_text: The RECOMMENDED initial value for kReorderingThreshold is 3, based on TCP loss recovery [RFC5681] [RFC6675].
clauses.raw_text: The RECOMMENDED initial value for kReorderingThreshold is 3, based on TCP loss recovery [RFC5681] [RFC6675].

clauses.normalized_text: Some networks may exhibit higher degrees of reordering, causing a sender to detect spurious losses.
clauses.raw_text: Some networks may exhibit higher degrees of reordering, causing a sender to detect spurious losses.

clauses.normalized_text: Spuriously declaring packets lost leads to unnecessary retransmissions and may result in degraded performance due to the actions of the congestion controller upon detecting loss.
clauses.raw_text: Spuriously declaring packets lost leads to unnecessary retransmissions and may result in degraded performance due to the actions of the congestion controller upon detecting loss.

clauses.normalized_text: Implementers MAY use algorithms developed for TCP, such as TCP-NCR [RFC4653], to improve QUIC’s reordering resilience.
clauses.raw_text: Implementers MAY use algorithms developed for TCP, such as TCP-NCR [RFC4653], to improve QUIC’s reordering resilience.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC implementations can use time-based loss detection to handle reordering based on time elapsed since the packet was sent.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC implementations can use time-based loss detection to handle reordering based on time elapsed since the packet was sent.

clauses.normalized_text: This may be used either as a replacement for a packet reordering threshold or in addition to it.
clauses.raw_text: This may be used either as a replacement for a packet reordering threshold or in addition to it.

clauses.normalized_text: The RECOMMENDED time threshold, expressed as a fraction of the round-trip time (kTimeReorderingFraction), is 1/8.
clauses.raw_text: The RECOMMENDED time threshold, expressed as a fraction of the round-trip time (kTimeReorderingFraction), is 1/8.

clauses.normalized_text: Unacknowledged packets close to the tail may have fewer than kReorderingThreshold retransmittable packets sent after them.
clauses.raw_text: Unacknowledged packets close to the tail may have fewer than kReorderingThreshold retransmittable packets sent after them.

clauses.normalized_text: Loss of such packets cannot be detected via Fast Retransmit.
clauses.raw_text: Loss of such packets cannot be detected via Fast Retransmit.

clauses.normalized_text: To enable ack-based loss detection of such packets, receipt of an acknowledgment for the last outstanding retransmittable packet triggers the Early Retransmit process, as follows.
clauses.raw_text: To enable ack-based loss detection of such packets, receipt of an acknowledgment for the last outstanding retransmittable packet triggers the Early Retransmit process, as follows.

clauses.normalized_text: If there are unacknowledged in-flight packets still pending, they should be marked as lost. To compensate for the reduced reordering resilience, the sender SHOULD set a timer for a small period of time.
clauses.raw_text: If there are unacknowledged in-flight packets still pending, they should be marked as lost. To compensate for the reduced reordering resilience, the sender SHOULD set a timer for a small period of time.

clauses.normalized_text: If the unacknowledged in-flight packets are not acknowledged during this time, then these packets MUST be marked as lost.
clauses.raw_text: If the unacknowledged in-flight packets are not acknowledged during this time, then these packets MUST be marked as lost.

clauses.normalized_text: An endpoint SHOULD set the timer such that a packet is marked as lost no earlier than 1.125 * max(SRTT, latest_RTT) since when it was sent.
clauses.raw_text: An endpoint SHOULD set the timer such that a packet is marked as lost no earlier than 1.125 * max(SRTT, latest_RTT) since when it was sent.

clauses.normalized_text: Using max(SRTT, latest_RTT) protects from the two following cases:
clauses.raw_text: Using max(SRTT, latest_RTT) protects from the two following cases:

clauses.normalized_text: the latest RTT sample is lower than the SRTT, perhaps due to reordering where packet whose ack triggered the Early Retransit process encountered a shorter path;
clauses.raw_text: the latest RTT sample is lower than the SRTT, perhaps due to reordering where packet whose ack triggered the Early Retransit process encountered a shorter path;

clauses.normalized_text: the latest RTT sample is higher than the SRTT, perhaps due to a sustained increase in the actual RTT, but the smoothed SRTT has not yet caught up.
clauses.raw_text: the latest RTT sample is higher than the SRTT, perhaps due to a sustained increase in the actual RTT, but the smoothed SRTT has not yet caught up.

clauses.normalized_text: The 1.125 multiplier increases reordering resilience.
clauses.raw_text: The 1.125 multiplier increases reordering resilience.

clauses.normalized_text: Implementers MAY experiment with using other multipliers, bearing in mind that a lower multiplier reduces reordering resilience and increases spurious retransmissions, and a higher multipler increases loss recovery delay.
clauses.raw_text: Implementers MAY experiment with using other multipliers, bearing in mind that a lower multiplier reduces reordering resilience and increases spurious retransmissions, and a higher multipler increases loss recovery delay.

clauses.normalized_text: This mechanism is based on Early Retransmit for TCP [RFC5827].
clauses.raw_text: This mechanism is based on Early Retransmit for TCP [RFC5827].

clauses.normalized_text: However, [RFC5827] does not include the timer described above.
clauses.raw_text: However, [RFC5827] does not include the timer described above.

clauses.normalized_text: Early Retransmit is prone to spurious retransmissions due to its reduced reordering resilence without the timer.
clauses.raw_text: Early Retransmit is prone to spurious retransmissions due to its reduced reordering resilence without the timer.

clauses.normalized_text: This observation led Linux TCP implementers to implement a timer for TCP as well, and this document incorporates this advancement.
clauses.raw_text: This observation led Linux TCP implementers to implement a timer for TCP as well, and this document incorporates this advancement.

clauses.normalized_text: Timer-based loss detection recovers from losses that cannot be handled by ack-based loss detection.
clauses.raw_text: Timer-based loss detection recovers from losses that cannot be handled by ack-based loss detection.

clauses.normalized_text: It uses a single timer which switches between a handshake retransmission timer, a Tail Loss Probe timer and Retransmission Timeout mechanisms.
clauses.raw_text: It uses a single timer which switches between a handshake retransmission timer, a Tail Loss Probe timer and Retransmission Timeout mechanisms.

clauses.normalized_text: Data in CRYPTO frames is critical to QUIC transport and crypto negotiation, so a more aggressive timeout is used to retransmit it.
clauses.raw_text: Data in CRYPTO frames is critical to QUIC transport and crypto negotiation, so a more aggressive timeout is used to retransmit it.

clauses.normalized_text: Below, the term “handshake packet” is used to refer to packets containing CRYPTO frames, not packets with the specific long header packet type Handshake.
clauses.raw_text: Below, the term “handshake packet” is used to refer to packets containing CRYPTO frames, not packets with the specific long header packet type Handshake.

clauses.normalized_text: The initial handshake timeout SHOULD be set to twice the initial RTT.
clauses.raw_text: The initial handshake timeout SHOULD be set to twice the initial RTT.

clauses.normalized_text: At the beginning, there are no prior RTT samples within a connection.
clauses.raw_text: At the beginning, there are no prior RTT samples within a connection.

clauses.normalized_text: Resumed connections over the same network SHOULD use the previous connection’s final smoothed RTT value as the resumed connection’s initial RTT.
clauses.raw_text: Resumed connections over the same network SHOULD use the previous connection’s final smoothed RTT value as the resumed connection’s initial RTT.

clauses.normalized_text: If no previous RTT is available, or if the network changes, the initial RTT SHOULD be set to 100ms.
clauses.raw_text: If no previous RTT is available, or if the network changes, the initial RTT SHOULD be set to 100ms.

clauses.normalized_text: When CRYPTO frames are sent, the sender SHOULD set a timer for the handshake timeout period.
clauses.raw_text: When CRYPTO frames are sent, the sender SHOULD set a timer for the handshake timeout period.

clauses.normalized_text: Upon timeout, the sender MUST retransmit all unacknowledged CRYPTO data by calling RetransmitAllUnackedHandshakeData().
clauses.raw_text: Upon timeout, the sender MUST retransmit all unacknowledged CRYPTO data by calling RetransmitAllUnackedHandshakeData().

clauses.normalized_text: On each consecutive expiration of the handshake timer without receiving an acknowledgement for a new packet, the sender SHOULD double the handshake timeout and set a timer for this period.
clauses.raw_text: On each consecutive expiration of the handshake timer without receiving an acknowledgement for a new packet, the sender SHOULD double the handshake timeout and set a timer for this period.

clauses.normalized_text: When CRYPTO frames are outstanding, the TLP and RTO timers are not active unless the CRYPTO frames were sent at 1RTT encryption.
clauses.raw_text: When CRYPTO frames are outstanding, the TLP and RTO timers are not active unless the CRYPTO frames were sent at 1RTT encryption.

clauses.normalized_text: When an acknowledgement is received for a handshake packet, the new RTT is computed and the timer SHOULD be set for twice the newly computed smoothed RTT.
clauses.raw_text: When an acknowledgement is received for a handshake packet, the new RTT is computed and the timer SHOULD be set for twice the newly computed smoothed RTT.

clauses.normalized_text: A Retry or Version Negotiation packet causes a client to send another Initial packet, effectively restarting the connection process.
clauses.raw_text: A Retry or Version Negotiation packet causes a client to send another Initial packet, effectively restarting the connection process.

clauses.normalized_text: Either packet indicates that the Initial was received but not processed.
clauses.raw_text: Either packet indicates that the Initial was received but not processed.

clauses.normalized_text: Neither packet can be treated as an acknowledgment for the Initial, but they MAY be used to improve the RTT estimate.
clauses.raw_text: Neither packet can be treated as an acknowledgment for the Initial, but they MAY be used to improve the RTT estimate.

clauses.normalized_text: The algorithm described in this section is an adaptation of the Tail Loss Probe algorithm proposed for TCP [TLP].
clauses.raw_text: The algorithm described in this section is an adaptation of the Tail Loss Probe algorithm proposed for TCP [TLP].

clauses.normalized_text: A packet sent at the tail is particularly vulnerable to slow loss detection, since acks of subsequent packets are needed to trigger ack-based detection.
clauses.raw_text: A packet sent at the tail is particularly vulnerable to slow loss detection, since acks of subsequent packets are needed to trigger ack-based detection.

clauses.normalized_text: To ameliorate this weakness of tail packets, the sender schedules a timer when the last retransmittable packet before quiescence is transmitted.
clauses.raw_text: To ameliorate this weakness of tail packets, the sender schedules a timer when the last retransmittable packet before quiescence is transmitted.

clauses.normalized_text: Upon timeout, a Tail Loss Probe (TLP) packet is sent to evoke an acknowledgement from the receiver.
clauses.raw_text: Upon timeout, a Tail Loss Probe (TLP) packet is sent to evoke an acknowledgement from the receiver.

clauses.normalized_text: The timer duration, or Probe Timeout (PTO), is set based on the following conditions:
clauses.raw_text: The timer duration, or Probe Timeout (PTO), is set based on the following conditions:

clauses.normalized_text: PTO SHOULD be scheduled for max(1.5*SRTT+MaxAckDelay, kMinTLPTimeout)
clauses.raw_text: PTO SHOULD be scheduled for max(1.5*SRTT+MaxAckDelay, kMinTLPTimeout)
